title: Edge Telemetry Aggregator and Label Contracts for Inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement an edge-side telemetry aggregator (lightweight sidecar) that harmonizes Prometheus scrape metrics and OTLP exports from inference runtime components into a contract-driven envelope for downstream ingestion. Motivation: reduce cardinality and telemetry egress costs from Dedicated/Private nodes, improve trace->metric correlation for LLM inference KPIs (latency_p50/p95, token_generation_errors, cold_start_count), and provide a stable label contract so downstream pipelines can perform reliable SLO rollups. The aggregator must support tenant scoping, sampling rules, histogram bucketing, delta counters, and deterministic label normalization without changing runtime metric instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Edge sidecar binary deployed to canary Dedicated pool and receives OTLP/Prometheus metrics from runtime instances
Sidecar applies label contract: (model_family, model_version, route, tenant_id, shard_region) and strips any high-cardinality labels not in contract
Telemetry proxies to central ingestion via Prometheus remote_write for aggregated gauges/counters and OTLP for exemplars/traces within our retention policy
End-to-end dashboards show <10% increase in 99th percentile ingestion latency and a >=3x reduction in unique label cardinality for canary tenant
Integration tests validate delta counter semantics and histogram bucket consistency
Config flags enable per-tenant sampling and a fallback that routes to cloud-side pipeline on sidecar failure
design_decisions: Use a hybrid model: scrape-based Prometheus receiver for legacy metrics plus OTLP gRPC for exemplar-rich traces and sparse metrics to preserve exemplars
Perform deterministic label canonicalization in sidecar with a allowlist contract to control cardinality and avoid downstream schema churn
Export aggregated time-series at 10s scrape interval to align with existing SLO windowing; preserve high-resolution exemplars streamed via OTLP
Sampling policy: keep 100% of requests for 'high-value' tenants until 1M tokens/day then switch to rate-based exemplar sampling; others get reservoir-based exemplar retention
Delta counters implemented in sidecar to convert monotonic cumulative counters into per-interval deltas for remote_write to reduce storage and enable rate SLO calculations
Prefer protobuf-based OTLP for traces and exemplars; use Prometheus remote_write for bulk metric aggregation due to compression and existing ingestion pipeline compatibility
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype sidecar receiver that accepts Prometheus scrapes and OTLP gRPC, apply label contract and emit to local memory store
Week 2: Implement aggregation + delta conversion and add config-driven sampling/policy engine
Week 3: Integrate exporters (remote_write + OTLP) and end-to-end CI with a canary Dedicated pool
Week 4: Create dashboards (latency/error SLOs), run workload tests, measure cardinality and ingestion load reductions
Week 5: Rollout plan: staged canary -> 25% pools -> full Dedicated; create rollback metrics and runbook
Follow-up: Add RBAC tagging for private deployments and encryption at rest integration with KMS
risks: Improper label stripping could drop useful dimensions causing SLO blindspots
Sidecar becomes single point of failure for telemetry if not properly isolated; must run with local buffering and fail-open behavior
Sampling misconfiguration could bias exemplars and degrade root-cause analysis fidelity
Performance overhead on Dedicated nodes might increase CPU usage; need limits and cgroups for sidecar
Schema drift risk: need strict versioning and migration strategy for label contracts
